All observations made on 2026-08-10 (~19:40–19:55 UTC, TZ=UTC) against working
fixture notebooks built by `/tmp/fixture/mkfull.sh` (fixture DB + the default
`.zk/config.toml` and `.zk/templates/default.md` from `zk init`, whose content is
`# {{title}}\n\n{{content}}\n`). Raw probe notebooks live under `/tmp/work-new/`.

CLI surface (from `--help`):

```
Usage: zk new [<directory>]
  -i, --interactive            Read contents from standard input.
  -t, --title=TITLE            Title of the new note.
      --date=DATE              Set the current date.
  -g, --group=NAME             Name of the config group this note belongs to.
      --extra=KEY=VALUE,...    Extra variables passed to the templates.
      --template=PATH          Custom template used to render the note.
  -p, --print-path             Print the path of the created note instead of editing it.
  -n, --dry-run                Don't actually create the note. Prints content on stdout, path on stderr.
      --id=ID                  Skip id generation and use provided value.
```

## 1. Default flow

`EDITOR=true zk new --no-input` in a notebook root:

- Generates a random id (default: **4 chars, alphanum `[a-z0-9]`, lowercase**),
  creates `<id>.md` in the target directory (cwd, or `<directory>` arg).
- Content = rendered content template. With default template and no title:
  exact bytes `# Untitled\n\n\n` (title defaults to `Untitled`; `{{content}}`
  empty; template's trailing `\n` kept). **No frontmatter is ever added.**
- The note is **indexed immediately** — inserted into `notes` table even if the
  editor step afterwards fails (see §3). Index `created`/`modified` use real
  wall-clock time, NOT `--date`.
- `--no-input` does NOT suppress the editor.
- With a title: `zk new -t "Hello World" --print-path` → file content
  `# Hello World\n\n\n`, stdout `/abs/path/j2qu.md\n`, exit 0.
- Default title is used when `-t ""` (empty string) too.

## 2. Output modes

- `--print-path`: prints the **absolute** path + `\n` to stdout, nothing to
  stderr, exit 0. No editor is launched. File is created and indexed.
- `--dry-run`: does NOT create any file and does NOT touch the index. Writes
  the exact would-be file bytes to **stdout**, and the absolute path + `\n` to
  **stderr**. Exit 0. `--print-path --dry-run` together behaves exactly like
  `--dry-run`.
- Extra positional arg: `zk new a b` → stderr `zk: error: unexpected argument b\n`, exit 1.
- Outside any notebook: `zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in /tmp or a parent directory\n`, exit 1.

## 3. Editor

After the file is created **and indexed**, zk launches the editor unless
`--print-path`/`--dry-run`. Resolution precedence:

1. `[tool] editor = "..."` in config (highest)
2. `$VISUAL`
3. `$EDITOR` (empty string counts as unset)

If none set: file is still created and indexed, then stderr
`zk: error: no editor set in config\n`, exit 1.

The editor command string is split on spaces and the absolute note path is
appended; it is run through a shell that redirects to `/dev/tty`. In a
TTY-less environment every editor invocation fails; observed stderr:

```
--: line 1: /dev/tty: No such device or address
zk: error: operation aborted by editor: code -w /tmp/work-new/n1/ot77.md: exit status 1
```

(exit 1; the `--: line 1:` line comes from the spawned shell). The full editor
string incl. args is echoed in the error (`true`, `vim`, `code -w`,
`myeditor --flag` all observed). The created file remains on disk and stays
indexed with the pre-edit content.

Under a pty (`script -qec ...`), `EDITOR=true` succeeds: exit 0, zk prints
nothing. **Edits made by the editor are NOT re-indexed**: an editor that
replaced the file content left the DB row with the original pre-edit title.

## 4. `--id` and id generation / collisions

- `--id=myid42` → creates `myid42.md`. `--id=foo.md` → `foo.md.md` (extension
  always appended). `--id=a/b` → creates subdirectory `a/` with `b.md`.
- `--id=` (empty) → falls back to random id generation.
- **Collision (file exists): silently opens the existing note.** Exit 0,
  `--print-path` prints the existing path, file content is NOT modified (even
  with `-i` stdin content — stdin is read but discarded), title flag ignored.
  Without `--print-path` the editor is launched on the existing file.
- **Collision + `--dry-run`: this is the only case that errors** — stdout
  empty, stderr:
  `zk: error: new note: /abs/path/alpha.md: note already exists\n`, exit 1.
- Random-id collisions behave the same: with `id-charset="ab"`, `id-length=1`,
  after `a.md` and `b.md` exist, further `zk new` runs randomly return one of
  the existing files, exit 0, content discarded. No retry-limit error observed.
- `id-length = -1` → **Go panic**, exit 2, stdout empty, stderr starts with
  `panic: IDOptions.Length must be at least 1` followed by a goroutine stack
  trace (reveals `internal/util/rand/rand.go:15`,
  `internal/core/notebook.go:150 NewNote`, `internal/cli/cmd/new.go:53`,
  kong v0.5.0, go1.24.0). `id-length = 0` → silently uses default 4.
- `id-charset`: `letters` → `[a-z]`; `numbers` → `[0-9]`; `alphanum`;
  `hex` → `[0-9a-f]`; any other string (incl. `"Alphanum"`, `"xyz_"`) is a
  custom charset; `""` → default alphanum.
- `id-case`: `lower` (default) / `upper` (uppercases custom charsets too, e.g.
  charset `ab1` + upper → `1ABA`) / `mixed`. Invalid value (e.g. `weird`) →
  silently behaves as `lower`.

## 5. `--date` (natural-language date parser)

Sets the value of `now` in templates; does NOT affect index created/modified.
Observed with today = 2026-08-10 UTC:

| input | `{{format-date now}}` |
|---|---|
| `2024-01-15` | `2024-01-15` |
| `2024-01-15T10:30:00` | `2024-01-15` (time dropped) |
| `tomorrow` / `yesterday` / `today` | `2026-08-11` / `2026-08-09` / `2026-08-10` |
| `monday` | `2026-08-03` (previous; 2026-08-10 is a Monday) |
| `next friday` | `2026-08-14` |
| `next week` / `last week` | `2026-08-17` / `2026-08-03` |
| `next month` / `last month` | `2026-09-10` / `2026-07-10` |
| `next year` / `last year` | `2027-08-10` / `2025-08-10` |
| `in 3 days` / `3 days ago` / `2 weeks ago` | `2026-08-13` / `2026-08-07` / `2026-07-27` |
| `sunday` / `next monday` / `last monday` | `2026-08-09` / `2026-08-17` / `2026-08-03` |
| `10:30` | `0000-01-01` (time-only → zero date!) |
| `december 25` | `2025-12-11` (garbage — recorded verbatim) |
| `dec 25` | `2026-08-11` (garbage — recorded verbatim) |
| `Jan 15 2024`, `15 Jan 2024` | `2026-11-02` (garbage — recorded verbatim) |
| `bogus`, `""` | silently = today (no error) |

Unparseable inputs that *start like* a grammar token → exit 1, stdout empty,
stderr exactly (11-space indents):

```
zk: error: 
           parse error near PegText (line 1 symbol 1 - line 1 symbol 5):
           "2024"
           
```

(trailing line is 11 spaces + `\n`). Triggered by `2024-13-45`, `2024/01/15`,
`25/12/2024`, `2024-1-5` (needs zero-padding), ` 2024-01-15` (leading space;
reported as `symbol 2 - line 1 symbol 6`), `2024-01-15 junk`.

## 6. `{{format-date}}` helper formats

`{{format-date now}}` → `2024-01-15`. Second arg is a format: named presets
`short` → `01/15/2024`, `medium` → `Jan 15, 2024`, `long` → `January 15, 2024`,
`full` → `Monday, January 15, 2024`, `time` → `00:00`, `timestamp` →
`202401150000`, `elapsed` → `3 years ago`, `year` → `2024`; otherwise
strftime-style `%` verbs work: `%Y %m %d %H %M %S %A %B %s` (epoch, UTC)
all verified. Unknown plain strings pass through literally (`iso` → `iso`,
`yyyy-MM-dd` → `yyyy-MM-dd`). `language = "fr"` did NOT localize any of these
(all stayed English). The old `{{date ...}}` helper hard-errors, exit 1:

```
zk: the {{date}} template helper was renamed to {{format-date}}, please update your configuration
```

## 7. Title → slug rules (`{{slug title}}`)

Verified outputs: `Hello World`→`hello-world`; case lowered; runs of
spaces→single `-`; `with-dash_and_underscore`→`with-dash_and_underscore`
(underscore kept); `: , . ! ? ( ) [ ] ' "` each become separators/dropped,
runs collapse (`punct: a,b.c!d?e(f)g[h]`→`punct-a-b-c-d-e-f-g-h`,
`dots...`→`dots`); apostrophe between letters is deleted with NO separator
(`don't stop`→`dont-stop`, `it's a test`→`its-a-test`); `&`→`and` inlined
(`a&b`→`aandb`, `C++ & C#`→`c-and-c`); `@`→`at` (`a@b`→`aatb`); `% + # $ * = ~ ^ | \ /`
→ separators (`a/b/c`→`a-b-c`, slug never creates subdirs); accents
transliterated (`unicode éèê café`→`unicode-eee-cafe`,
`Müller Ölberg Übung`→`muller-olberg-ubung`, `naïve façade`→`naive-facade`);
emoji dropped (`emoji 🎉 party`→`emoji-party`); CJK romanized
(`日本語 タイトル`→`ri-ben-yu-taitoru`); `100% sure`→`100-sure`.
Empty slug is legal: `-t "!!!"` creates a file literally named `.md`.
Very long names: exit 1, stderr
`zk: error: new note: stat xxxx…(300 x's).md: file name too long\n`.

## 8. Filename templates (`[note] filename`)

Default `"{{id}}"`. Handlebars-style syntax (raymond lexer; unclosed
`{{title` → exit 1: `zk: error: new note: load template failed: Parse error on line 1:\n           Lexer error\n           Token: Error{"Unclosed expression"}\n`).
Unknown variables AND unknown helpers render as empty string silently
(`{{unknownvar}}`, `{{foo title}}` → `.md`, exit 0).
`{{title}}` is raw (spaces/case kept: `Raw Title Here.md`). Slashes in the
rendered filename create subdirectories: `dir/{{id}}` → `dir/pkas.md`;
`{{format-date now "short"}}` → `01/15/2024.md` (dirs `01/15/` created).
`{{extra.key}}` works in filename templates. Available filename-template vars
observed: `id`, `title`, `slug` helper, `format-date` helper, `extra` map,
`now` (raw Go `time.Time` String: `2026-08-10 19:53:52.044375556 +0000 UTC m=+0.015207973`).

Content-template vars: `id`, `title`, `content`, `filename` (with extension),
`dir` (rel dir, `sub2`; empty at root), `path` (always empty for new notes),
`now`, `extra` map, `env` (map of the FULL process environment — `{{env}}`
dumps a Go `map[...]`; zk sets `ZK_NOTEBOOK_DIR` and `ZK_SHELL` in it).
Helpers: `slug`, `format-date`, `sh` (runs shell command, stdout inlined).
A failing `{{sh "exit 3"}}` prints `zk: {{sh}} command failed: exit status 3`
to stderr but is NON-fatal (exit 0, note created). Wrong helper arity → exit 1,
e.g. `zk: error: new note: render template failed: Evaluation error: Helper 'date' called with wrong number of arguments, needed 2 but got 0\n           Current node:\n           \tExpr{...}`.

## 9. `--extra`

Repeatable and comma-separated (`--extra k1=v1 --extra k2=w` ≡
`--extra k1=v1,k2=w`). Value may contain `=` (`--extra k2=a=b=c` → `a=b=c`).
Empty value ok. Last duplicate key wins. Access via `{{extra.k1}}`; missing
keys render empty. Merged over `[extra]` config section; `--extra` overrides
config. Malformed pair: `zk: error: --extra: expected "<key>=<value>" but got "novalue"\n`, exit 1.

## 10. `--template` / `[note] template`

- Relative paths resolve ONLY against `.zk/templates/` (a file in cwd is not
  found). Absolute paths work.
- Missing template: `zk: error: new note: load template file failed: cannot find template at nope.md\n`, exit 1 (abs path echoed verbatim).
- `~` expansion happens via the OS user database (→ `/root/...`), NOT `$HOME`.
- If the notebook has NO config at all and `.zk/templates/default.md` is
  missing, the note is created **empty (0 bytes)** with no error.

## 11. `-i/--interactive`

Reads ALL of stdin into `{{content}}`. `printf 'line one\nline two\n' | zk new
-i -t X` → `# X\n\nline one\nline two\n\n` (content + template trailing `\n`).
Empty stdin fine. Works with `--dry-run` and `--print-path`. Without `-i`,
piped stdin is ignored entirely (no title prompt on non-TTY; EOF also fine —
title falls back to `Untitled` silently, no prompt text on any stream).

## 12. Groups

```toml
[group."journal"]
paths = ["journal", "diary"]
[group."journal".note]
filename = "..."
[group."journal".extra]
```

- A `[directory]` arg (or cwd) under any listed path — including nested
  subdirs (`journal/sub`) — selects that group; group `[note]`/`[extra]`
  settings merge over global ones (unspecified keys, e.g. `extension`,
  inherit from global `[note]`).
- Omitting `paths` ⇒ implicitly `paths = ["<group name>"]`.
- `-g NAME` forces the group regardless of directory (takes precedence over
  path-derived group); the note is still created in the cwd/dir-arg location,
  not in the group's paths.
- Unknown group: `zk: error: new note: no group named \`nosuch\` found in the config\n`, exit 1.
- Nonexistent or non-directory `[directory]` arg:
  `zk: error: new note: nodir: directory not found\n`, exit 1 (same message for
  a file path).

## 13. Misc config interactions

- `[note] extension` changes the suffix (`5mzm.txt`, `fsf8.mdx`); appended to
  `--id` and filename templates alike.
- `[note] default-title = "My Default"` replaces `Untitled`.
- `[note] exclude` does NOT apply to `zk new`: a note created under an
  excluded glob (`drafts/*`) is created AND indexed normally.
- `[note] language = "fr"` showed no observable effect on slugs or date
  formats.
- `-W/--working-dir PATH` works (note created relative to that dir).
- `--notebook-dir PATH` from a cwd outside that notebook:
  `zk: error: new note: /tmp: path is outside the notebook at /tmp/work-new/nvars\n`, exit 1.
- New note in a subdirectory cwd (no dir arg) lands in that subdirectory;
  group selection follows that location.
- Title may contain newlines; rendered raw into the template.

## 14. Index state after `new`

- Created note is inserted into `notes` (path, title, created, modified with
  real timestamps, e.g. `2026-08-10 19:47:16.457980604+00:00`) BEFORE the
  editor runs; present even when the editor aborts or no editor is set.
- NOT re-indexed after the editor exits (post-edit content stays unindexed).
- `--dry-run` leaves the index untouched.

Empty slug is legal: `-t "!!!"` creates a file literally named `.md`.
Very long names: exit 1, stderr
`zk: error: new note: stat xxxx…(300 x's).md: file name too long\n`.

## 8. Filename templates (`[note] filename`)

Default `"{{id}}"`. Handlebars-style syntax (raymond lexer; unclosed
`{{title` → exit 1: `zk: error: new note: load template failed: Parse error on line 1:\n           Lexer error\n           Token: Error{"Unclosed expression"}\n`).
Unknown variables AND unknown helpers render as empty string silently
(`{{unknownvar}}`, `{{foo title}}` → `.md`, exit 0).
`{{title}}` is raw (spaces/case kept: `Raw Title Here.md`). Slashes in the
rendered filename create subdirectories: `dir/{{id}}` → `dir/pkas.md`;
`{{format-date now "short"}}` → `01/15/2024.md` (dirs `01/15/` created).
`{{extra.key}}` works in filename templates. Available filename-template vars
observed: `id`, `title`, `slug` helper, `format-date` helper, `extra` map,
`now` (raw Go `time.Time` String: `2026-08-10 19:53:52.044375556 +0000 UTC m=+0.015207973`).

Content-template vars: `id`, `title`, `content`, `filename` (with extension),
`dir` (rel dir, `sub2`; empty at root), `path` (always empty for new notes),
`now`, `extra` map, `env` (map of the FULL process environment — `{{env}}`
dumps a Go `map[...]`; zk sets `ZK_NOTEBOOK_DIR` and `ZK_SHELL` in it).
Helpers: `slug`, `format-date`, `sh` (runs shell command, stdout inlined).
A failing `{{sh "exit 3"}}` prints `zk: {{sh}} command failed: exit status 3`
to stderr but is NON-fatal (exit 0, note created). Wrong helper arity → exit 1,
e.g. `zk: error: new note: render template failed: Evaluation error: Helper 'date' called with wrong number of arguments, needed 2 but got 0\n           Current node:\n           \tExpr{...}`.

## 9. `--extra`

Repeatable and comma-separated (`--extra k1=v1 --extra k2=w` ≡
`--extra k1=v1,k2=w`). Value may contain `=` (`--extra k2=a=b=c` → `a=b=c`).
Empty value ok. Last duplicate key wins. Access via `{{extra.k1}}`; missing
keys render empty. Merged over `[extra]` config section; `--extra` overrides
config. Malformed pair: `zk: error: --extra: expected "<key>=<value>" but got "novalue"\n`, exit 1.

## 10. `--template` / `[note] template`

- Relative paths resolve ONLY against `.zk/templates/` (a file in cwd is not
  found). Absolute paths work.
- Missing template: `zk: error: new note: load template file failed: cannot find template at nope.md\n`, exit 1 (abs path echoed verbatim).
- `~` expansion happens via the OS user database (→ `/root/...`), NOT `$HOME`.
- If the notebook has NO config at all and `.zk/templates/default.md` is
  missing, the note is created **empty (0 bytes)** with no error.

## 11. `-i/--interactive`

Reads ALL of stdin into `{{content}}`. `printf 'line one\nline two\n' | zk new
-i -t X` → `# X\n\nline one\nline two\n\n` (content + template trailing `\n`).
Empty stdin fine. Works with `--dry-run` and `--print-path`. Without `-i`,
piped stdin is ignored entirely (no title prompt on non-TTY; EOF also fine —
title falls back to `Untitled` silently, no prompt text on any stream).

## 12. Groups

```toml
[group."journal"]
paths = ["journal", "diary"]
[group."journal".note]
filename = "..."
[group."journal".extra]
```

- A `[directory]` arg (or cwd) under any listed path — including nested
  subdirs (`journal/sub`) — selects that group; group `[note]`/`[extra]`
  settings merge over global ones (unspecified keys, e.g. `extension`,
  inherit from global `[note]`).
- Omitting `paths` ⇒ implicitly `paths = ["<group name>"]`.
- `-g NAME` forces the group regardless of directory (takes precedence over
  path-derived group); the note is still created in the cwd/dir-arg location,
  not in the group's paths.
- Unknown group: `zk: error: new note: no group named \`nosuch\` found in the config\n`, exit 1.
- Nonexistent or non-directory `[directory]` arg:
  `zk: error: new note: nodir: directory not found\n`, exit 1 (same message for
  a file path).

## 13. Misc config interactions

- `[note] extension` changes the suffix (`5mzm.txt`, `fsf8.mdx`); appended to
  `--id` and filename templates alike.
- `[note] default-title = "My Default"` replaces `Untitled`.
- `[note] exclude` does NOT apply to `zk new`: a note created under an
  excluded glob (`drafts/*`) is created AND indexed normally.
- `[note] language = "fr"` showed no observable effect on slugs or date
  formats.
- `-W/--working-dir PATH` works (note created relative to that dir).
- `--notebook-dir PATH` from a cwd outside that notebook:
  `zk: error: new note: /tmp: path is outside the notebook at /tmp/work-new/nvars\n`, exit 1.
- New note in a subdirectory cwd (no dir arg) lands in that subdirectory;
  group selection follows that location.
- Title may contain newlines; rendered raw into the template.

## 14. Index state after `new`

- Created note is inserted into `notes` (path, title, created, modified with
  real timestamps, e.g. `2026-08-10 19:47:16.457980604+00:00`) BEFORE the
  editor runs; present even when the editor aborts or no editor is set.
- NOT re-indexed after the editor exits (post-edit content stays unindexed).
- `--dry-run` leaves the index untouched.
